The '''2019–20 season''' was '''[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool Football Club]]''''s [[List of Liverpool F.C. seasons|128th season]] in existence and the club's 58th consecutive season in the top flight of English football. Liverpool also competed in the [[2019–20 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2019–20 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], [[2019 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]], [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], [[2019 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] and the [[2019 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]]. The season was suspended from 13 March to 17 June due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/1651836 |title=Premier League statement on impact of COVID-19 |date=5 April 2020 |publisher=Premier League |access-date=7 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11996065/premier-league-returns-on-june-17 |title=Premier League set to resume on June 17 |website=Sky Sports |date=28 May 2020 |access-date=28 May 2020}}</ref>

==Season overview==
Having finished second in the [[2018–19 Premier League]], Liverpool contested the 2019 FA Community Shield against [[Treble (association football)#Domestic trebles|domestic treble winners]] [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], losing 5–4 on penalties after a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49141690 |title=Community Shield: Liverpool 1–1 Man City (City won 5–4 on penalties) |first=Emlyn |last=Begley |publisher=BBC |date=4 August 2019 |access-date=11 October 2019}}</ref> As winners of the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League]], they contested the 2019 UEFA Super Cup against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], winning 5–4 on penalties after a 2–2 draw. The victory was Liverpool's fourth in the annual contest; only [[Real Madrid]], [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[AC Milan]] have more wins, with five titles apiece.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49332825 |title=Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties to win Super Cup |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=14 August 2019 |access-date=24 September 2019}}</ref>

Liverpool were eliminated in the quarter-finals of the 2019–20 EFL Cup by [[Aston Villa]] after fielding a vastly inexperienced side, managed by [[Liverpool F.C. Reserves and Academy|Liverpool under-23]] manager [[Neil Critchley]], while the first-team squad participated in the 2019 FIFA Club World Cup in Qatar under Klopp.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/liverpool-aston-villa-longstaff-kane-17430446 |title=Three Liverpool youngsters to watch out for against Aston Villa |last=Addison |first=Matt |date=17 December 2019 |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |access-date=17 December 2019}}</ref> Having finished as runners-up on three previous occasions, Liverpool won their first world title after defeating Brazilian club [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] 1–0 in the [[2019 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]] [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|after extra time]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Firmino winner seals Club World Cup win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50869633 |access-date=21 December 2019 |date=21 December 2019 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> making them the first English side to win the international treble of the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ladson |first1=Matt |title=What does Liverpool's Club World Cup victory mean for the rest of their season? |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/liverpools-club-world-cup-victory-win-premier-league-season-matt-ladson |access-date=22 December 2019 |website=FourFourTwo |date=22 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Eriksen |first1=Magnus |title=Liverpool do something no English club has done before with Club World Cup win |url=https://www.caughtoffside.com/2019/12/21/liverpool-first-english-team-to-win-cl-super-cup-and-club-world-cup/ |website=CaughtOffside |access-date=22 December 2019}}</ref> Liverpool were unsuccessful in their defence of the UEFA Champions League, exiting the competition in the round of 16 following a 4–2 aggregate defeat across two legs after extra time to [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51800660 |title=Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 3 |date=12 March 2020 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=25 March 2020}}</ref>

On 25 June, following [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]'s defeat to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], Liverpool clinched their nineteenth league title – the first since [[1989–90 Liverpool F.C. season|1989–90]] and the first during the Premier League era. Upon winning the league, Liverpool claimed the unusual achievement of winning the Premier League earlier than any other team by games played (with seven remaining) and later than any other team by date (being the only team to clinch the title in June).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mendola |first=Nicholas |date=25 June 2020 |title=Earliest Premier League champion: Is Liverpool fastest to clinch? |url=https://soccer.nbcsports.com/2020/06/25/earliest-premier-league-title-winners-in-history/ |access-date=25 June 2020 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

Over the season, Liverpool set a number of other [[Football records and statistics in England|English top-flight records]], including the most consecutive home wins (24; of which 7 were carried over from the previous season)<ref name=PMrecords>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1561869 |title=Which Premier League records have Liverpool set? |publisher=Premier League |access-date=26 July 2020}}</ref> and the biggest point lead at any time (25).<ref name=PMrecords/> They also matched the [[Premier League records and statistics|Premier League records]] for the most wins (32)<ref name=PMrecords/> the most home wins (18),<ref name=PMrecords/> and the most consecutive wins (18).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51623640 |title=Jurgen Klopp: Liverpool boss 'never thought' record would be equalled |website=BBC Sport |date=24 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2020/02/25/football/liverpool-record-premier-league-manchester-city-spt-intl/index.html |title=Liverpool continues its unbeaten streak to equal English Premier League record |publisher=CNN |date=25 February 2020}}</ref> Beginning the season prior, Liverpool enjoyed a 44-match unbeaten run in the league, the second-longest streak in top-flight history, behind [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s run of 49 games between May 2003 to October 2004.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://talksport.com/football/650791/liverpool-premier-league-title-win-record-crystal-palace/ |title=STAGGERING When can Liverpool win the Premier League? Reds on course to beat record for earliest title triumph with just FOUR more wins required |publisher=Talksport |date=25 February 2020}}</ref> The team remained unbeaten at home in the league for the third season in a row<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53412782 |title=Liverpool 5–3 Chelsea: Champions win thriller before receiving trophy |website=BBC Sport |date=26 July 2020}}</ref> and finished the season with 99 points, the club's record and the second highest in English top-flight history after Manchester City's 100 [[2017–18 Premier League|two years prior]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53460589 |title=Newcastle 1–3 Liverpool: Jurgen Klopp's side come from behind to win |website=BBC Sport |date=26 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/403883-2019-20-in-numbers-how-the-champions-broke-records-and-made-history|title=2019–20 in numbers, how the champions broke records and made history|date=31 July 2020|publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=4 August 2020}}</ref> Liverpool also recorded the best ever start to a season in the history of the [[UEFA coefficient#Men's Association coefficient|top 5 leagues in Europe]] (as they stood in 2020), picking up 20 wins and 1 draw for a total of 61 points out of a possible of 63;<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-01-12|title=The 15 best ever starts to a season after 21 games - and how each one ended|url=https://www.givemesport.com/1537230-liverpool-break-record-for-best-start-to-season-a-look-at-the-15-best-starts-in-europes-top-5-leagues|access-date=2021-02-21|website=GiveMeSport|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Jurgen Klopp says Liverpool not distracted by potential European record|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11669/11905009/jurgen-klopp-says-liverpool-not-distracted-by-potential-european-record|access-date=2021-04-02|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref> they eventually extended that record to 26 wins and 1 draw for a total of 79 points out of a possible 81 before suffering their first league defeat on 29 February 2020 to Watford.<ref>[https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51595064 Watford 3-0 Liverpool: Jurgen Klopp's side lose first Premier League game of the season]</ref>

=== FA Cup ===
{{main|2019–20 FA Cup}}

Liverpool entered the competition in the third round. The draw for the third round was made on 2 December 2019.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50637970 |title=FA Cup third round: Liverpool draw Everton in third round |date=2 December 2019 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=2 December 2019}}</ref> The fourth round draw was made by [[Alex Scott (footballer, born 1984)|Alex Scott]] and [[David O'Leary]] on Monday, 6 January 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=The Emirates FA Cup fourth round Draw Is Complete |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2020/jan/06/fa-cup-fourth-round-draw-060120 |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=8 January 2019}}</ref> The draw for the fifth round was made on 27 January 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51271468|title=FA Cup fifth-round draw: Wayne Rooney to face former side Man Utd|date=5 February 2020|work=BBC Sport|access-date=4 November 2020}}</ref>
